security_audit.summary: All 37 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, example links, or ordinary prose. A separate semantic review found one destructive Redis command presented without sufficient execution safeguards.

remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a non-destructive diagnostic procedure, or require explicit authorization, target verification, backup confirmation, and a service-specific runbook.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Redis Command Lacks Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: The quick reference presents redis-cli FLUSHDB as an emergency cache-clear command. It deletes the selected Redis database without target, backup, or authorization checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: FLUSHDB has documented destructive semantics, and the surrounding guidance provides only an emergency-only label rather than execution safeguards.

content.value_statement: Incomplete handoffs cause lost context and slower incident response. This skill provides structured templates, checklists, and escalation guidance for smooth shift transitions.
actual_capabilities: Creates detailed shift handoffs covering incidents, investigations, changes, known issues, and upcoming events.
Produces concise asynchronous handoffs for routine shift changes.
Structures mid-incident transfers with status, impact, mitigation, ownership, and next steps.
Provides outgoing, incoming, pre-shift, daily, and post-shift checklists.
Defines handoff meeting agendas and escalation triggers.
Suggests a timed overlap process for outgoing and incoming engineers.
limitations: It does not connect to monitoring, paging, chat, ticketing, or deployment systems.
Example links, names, dates, services, and incident identifiers are placeholders.
Teams must adapt severity rules, escalation paths, access checks, and response targets.
Operational commands require independent validation, authorization, and environment-specific safeguards.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Weekly Shift Handoff
use_cases.description: Turn current incidents, recent changes, and scheduled events into a complete transition document.

use_cases.title: Transfer an Active Incident
use_cases.description: Summarize current impact, mitigation progress, technical findings, ownership, and immediate next actions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Handoffs
use_cases.description: Create shared checklists, meeting agendas, escalation criteria, and documentation expectations for an on-call rotation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an on-call handoff from these notes: [notes]. Separate active incidents, investigations, recent changes, known issues, and upcoming events.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured handoff from unorganized notes.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Quick Async Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise asynchronous handoff from [notes]. Include a summary, watch list, recent changes, upcoming events, and clear owners.
prompt_templates.scenario: The shifts cannot schedule a live overlap meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer an Active Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a mid-incident handoff using [incident details]. Include impact, current state, evidence, completed actions, next steps, owners, and escalation conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An active incident continues across a shift boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Team Handoff Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an on-call handoff process for [team context]. Define timing, required sections, verification checks, escalation criteria, ownership, and quality controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a repeatable handoff standard.

output_examples.input: No active incidents. API latency investigation continues. Review backup-window logs tomorrow. Release 5.0 starts at 14:00 UTC.
output_examples.output: Summary: No active incidents. Watch API latency during the backup window. Review new logs tomorrow. Monitor release 5.0 from 14:00 UTC.

output_examples.input: Payment errors are 15 percent and falling. Pods scaled from five to fifteen. Escalate if errors remain above one percent.
output_examples.output: Current state: Payment errors are 15 percent and improving. Mitigation: Fifteen pods are active. Next step: Escalate if errors remain above one percent.

output_examples.input: Build a pre-shift readiness list for a new platform engineer.
output: Confirm paging ownership and receive a test alert.
Verify VPN, cluster, dashboard, log, and read-only database access.
Review recent incidents, critical runbooks, and escalation contacts.

best_practices: Use precise timestamps, owners, impact statements, and next actions.
Confirm access, alert routing, and understanding before the outgoing engineer leaves.
Link each investigation to current evidence, decisions, dashboards, runbooks, and tickets.
anti_patterns: Do not report status without naming an owner and next action.
Do not copy stale links, contacts, thresholds, or incident details into a new handoff.
Do not run example operational commands without authorization and environment validation.

faq.question: Does this skill integrate with PagerDuty or Slack?
faq.answer: No. It creates handoff content but does not connect to paging, chat, monitoring, or ticketing services.

faq.question: Can it prepare a handoff during an active incident?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize impact, current status, mitigation, evidence, owners, resources, and immediate next steps.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide active incidents, investigations, recent changes, known issues, upcoming events, contacts, resources, and escalation rules.

faq.question: Can teams customize the templates?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace examples with team-specific services, severity levels, access checks, escalation paths, schedules, and communication channels.

faq.question: Does it verify operational facts?
faq.answer: No. Users must validate status, ownership, links, metrics, access, and commands against current systems.

faq.question: Is a live handoff meeting required?
faq.answer: No. The skill supports asynchronous handoffs, but active or complex incidents benefit from direct confirmation between engineers.
